stories.text:
KSI, IF YOU'RE READING THIS — F* YOU! 🤬🖕 If I had only known what your promo would turn into...

Hi everyone. For those who don't know me: my name is Amelia, I'm 31, working as a regular cashier at Tesco in Luton, and I'm raising my 8-year-old daughter Lily all on my own.

No rich parents, no ex-husband sending child support. Just me. The rent on our damp flat — where there's black mold on the walls in winter and suffocating heat in summer — shot up to £1,100 a month. My wages with all overtime barely hit £1,500. When the massive British Gas bill came in last month, I looked at the numbers and panic literally made me sick. My chest tightened so hard I couldn't breathe.

Lately, I felt like I was losing my mind. Early shifts, late shifts, 12 hours on my feet scanning groceries for people always in a rush... I’d crawl home so exhausted I didn’t even have the strength to take off my boots. At night, when Lily fell asleep, I’d step out onto the freezing cold balcony and silently weep. So quietly, so she wouldn't hear me. All I begged God for was to stop counting pennies. To stop feeling that terrifying pit in my stomach every time the card machine at the till took too long to process my payment for cheap beans and bread... 😭

The moment I finally broke down happened over something small. Lily came home from school and timidly asked for £80 for a class trip to Alton Towers. And I had to say no. I told her: "Maybe next time, sweetie," and she just dropped her eyes, whispered: "Okay, mum," and walked to her room.

That night I sobbed in the kitchen like a madwoman. The soles on her winter boots were already peeling off, held together with duct tape, and I didn't even have a miserable eighty quid so my child could go with her friends. 💔

The next day during our tea break, my coworker Gemma shoved her phone in my face. "Amelia, how much longer are you gonna kill yourself for peanuts?" she asked.

She showed me a video of KSI. In the video, he was explaining how he partnered with developers to launch his official gaming app, KSI: Lucky Wheel, to give everyday Brits a chance to make decent money in these tough times. Gemma said she tried it just for a laugh and pulled out £1,200 over the weekend! She opened her Revolut app right in front of me and showed the bank transfer deposits...

I snapped back immediately: "Yeah right, just another internet scam." Honestly, it made me furious. But that thought kept eating away at my brain all day.

That evening, lying in bed, I was scrolling through TikTok and FB, and this promo was EVERYWHERE. Real people, videos, reviews — everyone shouting that KSI wasn't lying and cashouts were instant. I thought: what if I'm just a paranoid idiot denying myself the only lifeline out of this?

I downloaded KSI: Lucky Wheel before I could talk myself out of it. I deposited my last £20 — literally the money we were supposed to live on until Friday. I instantly got a welcome bonus from KSI: 255 free spins plus £200 in bonus funds. My hands were shaking like crazy. I felt like a criminal. 😳

I opened the main wheel game. My balance started climbing fast — £150, then £500, then £2,000... At one point it hit £3,400! I put £300 in for withdrawal just to test it. When a minute later my phone lit up with a Barclays notification confirming the transfer, I stopped breathing: "Wait... is this actually real?!"

And then I made a mistake. Greed took over, and I started raising the stakes. My balance tanked and stopped at £15. I locked my phone and lay in the dark, hating myself: "You absolute idiot! You blew your last money, serves you right!"

And then I remembered I still had those 255 free spins from KSI left.

That's when my life completely flipped upside down. A multiplier hit: x50... then x100... then x5000!!! The screen froze, flooded with golden coins. I stared at the numbers in disbelief. I closed and reopened the app ten times thinking it was a glitch. 🔥

On my balance was £87,400!!! OVER EIGHTY-SEVEN THOUSAND POUNDS! 🤯

I felt no joy in that moment. It was pure TERRIFYING FEAR. Fear that it was an error, that it would all vanish. With trembling fingers, I requested a withdrawal of the entire amount to my bank card.

The next morning, Barclays Fraud department called to verify an "anomalously large transaction". I was shaking from head to toe, but I explained it was an official app payout. The operator calmly replied: "Everything is fine, Amelia, the funds are cleared and available." When I hung up, I dropped my head onto the kitchen table and cried so hard I could barely catch my breath. 😭

The first thing I did was totally irrational. Instead of putting it straight into savings, I called in sick, grabbed Lily from school, and we went straight to Westfield Shopping Centre. I bought her the most expensive winter boots, a stylish coat she'd been eyeing, and right there from my phone, I transferred the money to her teacher for that school trip.

I stood in the middle of the shopping centre holding designer bags, crying like an idiot while my little girl jumped up and down in her new boots, asking worriedly why mum was crying. 👟🎒

Mum isn't crying from sadness, sweetheart. Mum is happy for the first time in years. ❤️

And as for you, KSI... That night when I was losing, I cursed your name. But today... today I want to say THANK YOU for pulling us out of that hell. 🙏

👇 UPDATE: So many people in the comments are asking what app this is. I can't reply to everyone, so I left the official link with those same 255 free spins from KSI in the first pinned comment! May you get as lucky as I did!
